status: concept draft for discussion, not deployed
source: Concept discussed in this BUS230 chat on 21–22 October; retained on 26 October

anna.name: Anna
anna.problem: “I know the steps, but I still don’t understand why we are replacing our paper records.”
anna.question: What should you ask first?
ask: “Which step of the scanning process is difficult?”
“What would help you understand the reason for the change?”
anna.evidence: Anna wants to understand the purpose. She is not asking for another procedure guide.
anna.actionQuestion: What should your team do next?
actions: Explain the stock-record problem, connect it to her work and invite questions.
anna.wrongAsk: Check what Anna is actually questioning: the reason for change, rather than the steps or the date.
anna.wrongAction: More instructions or a deadline do not answer the question about purpose.
anna.event: Anna joins the shift briefing and asks how the change will affect her daily work.
anna.note: Awareness support has started. Other readiness needs still require checking.

omar.name: Omar
omar.problem: “I support better records, but I am worried the new rating will blame me for old stock errors.”
omar.question: What evidence should you examine?
ask: Check which errors the rating rule includes and record his concern.
Ask whether Omar feels motivated enough.
Ask IT whether his account is active.
omar.evidence: The rating rule is disputed. The sponsor needs to check how inherited errors are treated.
omar.actionQuestion: What should your team do next?
actions: Promise the policy is fair before checking it.
Ask the sponsor to review the rule and communicate a reasoned decision.
omar.wrongAsk: Investigate the policy concern before assuming unwillingness or an access problem.
omar.wrongAction: Reassurance or motivation alone does not establish whether the rule is fair.
omar.event: A policy-review request reaches the operations sponsor, with the concern and an accountable owner.
omar.note: The response is pending. A request is not evidence that the policy has already changed.

mia.name: Mia
mia.problem: “The scanner works. I want to use the system, but I don’t know how to record a delivery mismatch.”
mia.question: What should you check first?
ask: Ask whether she supports the reason for change.
Schedule an independent task test immediately.
Ask whether the mismatch procedure has been explained and demonstrated.
mia.evidence: Mia has only been shown a normal delivery. The exception process has not been taught.
mia.actionQuestion: What should your team do next?
actions: Demonstrate a mismatch, guide practice and ask her to explain the steps.
Repeat why accurate stock records matter.
Ask her to try alone and review errors later.
mia.wrongAsk: Identify the missing instruction before asking for independent performance.
mia.wrongAction: Mia needs the procedure and supported practice before working independently.
mia.event: The manager and Mia work through a sample mismatch together.
mia.note: Explaining the steps supports Knowledge. Realistic performance is still needed to verify Ability.

leo.name: Leo
leo.problem: “I can explain the procedure, but I still cannot complete the task on my shift.”
leo.question: What should you investigate?
ask: Ask him to repeat his confidence score.
Check scanner reliability, practice time and realistic task evidence.
Check whether he remembers the launch date.
leo.evidence: The scanner is unreliable, there is no protected practice time, and the task has not been observed in usable conditions.
leo.actionQuestion: What should your team do next?
actions: Start the task with a supervisor and review errors afterwards.
Pause this task; allocate scanner repair and practice time, then observe a realistic attempt.
leo.wrongAsk: Self-report and deadlines do not establish whether the equipment, time and task evidence are adequate.
leo.wrongAction: An essential condition is missing. More training or supervision alone does not remove it.
leo.event: IT receives the scanner issue; the store manager protects practice time and schedules a task observation.
leo.note: Only the affected task stays paused. Ability remains unverified until conditions and performance are checked.

sara.name: Sara
sara.problem: “I used the system correctly in the pilot, but old paper forms are coming back.”
sara.question: What should you check first?
ask: Check whether equipment, knowledge or follow-up has changed.
Assume she needs the introductory course again.
Ask only whether she has seen the latest reminder.
sara.evidence: The equipment works and Sara knows the procedure. Reviews and feedback stopped after the pilot.
sara.actionQuestion: What should your team do next?
actions: Send another reminder and close the issue.
Arrange brief reviews, task-focused feedback and a way to raise new obstacles.
Book the same introductory course again.
sara.wrongAsk: Check the current barrier instead of assuming that earlier training has been forgotten.
sara.wrongAction: A reminder or repeat course alone does not supply the missing follow-up.
sara.event: A regular review and feedback conversation is added to the manager’s schedule.
sara.note: Reinforcement needs continuing support. Lasting adoption is not proved by a single reminder or review.
